members.tone: Approving and self-assured: elegance with a signature on it, where *elegance* alone can be impersonal.
The plain central name for the quality — gracefulness and good taste, with no dazzle asked of it.
The same stylish elegance with spirit in it, brisk and showy where *style* is merely distinctive.
Praises beauty that is fine rather than bold, the softest note in a family that runs to *grandeur*.
Elevated and imposing — splendour on a scale that asks to be looked up at.
Informal and flatly approving: elegance of dress or behaviour named in one blunt syllable.
Places the elegance in fineness of manner and expression, praising a person's polish rather than any effect they make.
Full-throated praise for the magnificent, glowing where *grandeur* towers.
Binds the splendour to ceremony, so the praise falls on the staging rather than on the thing staged.
The homelier name for beauty in fineness, prettier and less lofty in sound than *delicacy*.
Measures the elegance by fashion, approving of being current in a way *elegance* never is.
The largest word here — grandeur and splendour taken together at full strength, with nothing held back.
Magnificence that dazzles, adding glitter where *grandeur* adds height.
The British spelling of *splendor*, identical to it in force.
Ceremonial splendour with a flourish on it — the dazzle the occasion throws off, where *pomp* is the display itself.
